materials.label: Uruk IV administrative tablet VAT 14682
materials.what_audience_follows: A small one-sided Uruk IV tablet turns quantities of milk into an organized durable account, making visible how early writing could work before it encoded continuous speech.
sequence: A small clay tablet is prepared for a short administrative account.
Numerical and commodity signs are placed on one face to record quantities of milk.
The apparently drawn signs are produced through repeated impressions of a straight reed stylus.
The object preserves a structured relation among quantity, commodity and tablet position without requiring a recoverable sentence.

locators: Visible Language, Catalog No. 44, p. 73: VAT 14682, Uruk IV, Eana District; short account of milk quantities
Visible Language, Catalog No. 44 description: signs made by repeated impressions of a straight reed stylus

limitations: One tablet cannot represent the whole Uruk IV corpus.
Its layout and sign structure do not recover continuous speech or prove the underlying language.
Do not narrate the stylus technique as the already-mature wedge ductus of later cuneiform.

gaps: The current WS03 evidence supports the long technical shift toward more abstract/wedge-shaped cuneiform, but no single local source locator reconstructs that entire transformation as one continuous object sequence. Keep that long change explanatory unless later research adds a tighter comparative series.
